title: Checkpoint: How the Republic Worked
objective: After this level you can explain how consuls, Senate, assemblies and tribunes balanced one another.
summary: Consuls led, the Senate advised, the assemblies elected and legislated, and tribunes could veto: a mixed constitution Polybius admired.

cards.headline: Chapter 2 finale. How do you stop anyone from becoming a king?
cards.body: You spread power around and let each part hold the others back. Here’s the whole machine.

items.label: Consuls
points: Two, elected every year, each able to block the other

items.label: Citizens and tribunes
points: Assemblies elected magistrates and passed laws

cards.headline: Checks and balances
cards.body: It took an outsider to name the design. Polybius, a Greek historian taken to Rome as a hostage, wrote his history to explain how Rome came to dominate the Mediterranean world. Along the way he praised Rome’s government as a mix of three kinds of rule: the consuls were the monarchy, the Senate the aristocracy, and the assemblies the democracy. Each part checked the others, so none could take over. Rome kept a piece of a king, a piece of the nobles and a piece of the people, and let none of them win.

cards.headline: Chapter 2 complete
learned: The Senate advised, and was heeded
Assemblies elected and legislated; tribunes could veto

questions.prompt: In Rome’s assemblies, what did citizens do?

options.label: Advised the consuls on war
Tended the sacred fire
Elected magistrates and passed laws
Chose the next king

questions.explanation: Citizens met in assemblies to elect magistrates and pass laws.

questions.prompt: Which officials could block other magistrates with a single word?

options.label: The tribunes of the plebs
The senators
The augurs
The consuls’ lictors

questions.explanation: Tribunes could stop other magistrates, even consuls, by declaring “Veto.”

questions.prompt: Why did Polybius think Rome’s government was stable?

options.label: Rome had the largest army in the world
options.rationale: His point was about the constitution.

options.label: One wise ruler made every decision
The gods protected Rome’s laws
Each part of the government checked the others

questions.explanation: Consuls, Senate and assemblies each had power, and each held the others in check.

questions.prompt: Which change ended the Conflict of the Orders?

options.label: Plebeians were allowed to join the army
Plebeian assembly votes became binding on all Romans
Patricians were banned from the Senate
A plebeian was crowned king

questions.explanation: The Hortensian law of 287 BCE made the plebeian assembly’s votes binding on everyone.

questions.prompt: Chapter 2 recap: what links one-year consuls, the six-month dictatorship and Cincinnatus?

options.label: Power should be held only for a limited time
Power should pass from father to son
Power should belong to the priests
Power should go to the richest family

questions.explanation: Short terms and Cincinnatus’s early resignation all express the Republic’s rule: power is temporary.
